title: Notifyr — Push Notification Service
objective: Sending a notification requires a request signed with this service's secret, which the console never shows you. Send one anyway.

verifier.condition: A notification is sent with a signature computed using the secret read from a debug endpoint.

weakness: A `/debug/*` namespace added for local testing was never removed or gated by environment, and one of its endpoints echoes back the service's current HMAC signing secret.
seededData: An empty notification log. In memory; reset with the instance.
hints: Look for parts of the application that were never meant to be part of the product — not every route is linked from a page.
A service that signs its own requests has to keep that secret somewhere reachable by its own code. See whether anything exposes it.
Once you have the secret, compute an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the exact JSON body you want to send and attach it as the request asks.
burpNotes: Try a handful of short, guessable paths under a common prefix — Burp's Intruder with a small wordlist is the right tool.
